passages.actor_quote: Leising Spencer Bray Doriot Mishler Taylor

passages.provision_quote: Specifies requirements that apply to any action challenging the apportionment of congressional districts or general assembly districts.
passages.note: Operative content of the bill Bray voted against: the general assembly draws new congressional districts directly and the bill separately restricts how courts may review apportionment challenges, bundling the map-drawing clause with the court-oversight clause.

rows.reasoning: Bray voted Nay on final passage of HB 1032 (2026), which both has the general assembly draw new congressional districts and specifies new requirements restricting how courts may hear challenges to that apportionment. A No vote on this multi-clause instrument, with no statement tying it to one clause, shows only opposition to this particular bill; it does not establish whether Bray favors 'independent citizens' commissions with no elected officials involved at any level,' an 'independent redistricting commission,' a 'bipartisan legislative committee,' or 'state legislatures with court oversight to prevent extreme partisan bias' over the version of legislature-drawn, limited-court-review redistricting the bill would have enacted.
